newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower at day in the red.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower at day in the red.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Tuesday after trading in the red all day with every sector posting losses and the bourse depressed further by a weak opening on Wall Street.
The Stockholm general index ended 0.65 percent lower at 3,144.53, slipping off a record high close on Monday. Turnover was quiet with shares worth 3.23 billion crowns changing hands.
Brokers said rising interest rates dampened any enthusiasm.
Bearings maker SKF was in the spotlight, posting a slightly lower than expected profit of 1.10 billion crowns for the first half of 1997 against 1.48 billion crowns last year.
However its shares rose up to eight crowns to 220 after the company said improving trends of the second quarter were expected to continue over the rest of the year.
But the company did not announce any restructuring as speculated in the market. SKF shares ended flat at 212 crowns.
"We will not deliver a big rationalisation programme but a bag with a smaller package," SKF's managing director Peter Augustsson told Reuters.
One broker said: "The market reacted positively at first on the report but then recoiled in disappointment over the lack of a rationalisation programme."
A winner of the day was U.S./Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn that ended 3.5 higher at 288.5 crowns.
Brokers attributed P&U's gains to rises in New York overight Monday and a good sales report from Swiss drugs group Roche Holding.
Drugs major Astra ended one lower at 155 crowns.
Fellow market heavyweight, telecoms group Ericsson was 0.5 lower at 328.5 crowns.
